title: Opening the Dhammapada
hookLine: 423 verses in 26 chapters, "the path of dhamma"; the best-loved book of the Buddha's sayings

cards: If you've ever seen a Buddhist quote on a poster, a mug or a yoga studio wall, there's a fair chance it was claimed to come from one small book. Some of those quotes really are in it. Some are not in it at all.

The real book is short enough to read in an afternoon, and deep enough to keep coming back to. For the next seventy-five days, you and i will read it in order, a few verses at a time, so you'll know exactly what it says.

teach.b: The Dhammapada is four hundred twenty-three short verses in twenty-six chapters. It sits in the Pali Canon, in the part called the minor collection, but its verses are anything but minor in practice.
In Theravada countries it is memorized and chanted, and some people know dozens of verses by heart. The name has two halves. Dhamma you know: the teaching, and the way things truly are.

teach.h: PADA — FOOT, PATH, LINE OF VERSE.
teach.b: Pada has several meanings: a foot, a footstep, a path, and also a line of verse.
So Dhammapada can mean the path of the dhamma, the words of the dhamma, or the verses of the dhamma, and the tradition happily hears all of them at once.
Each verse is meant to be carried: short, rhythmic, easy to remember on a walk.
Each chapter gathers verses around one theme, with titles like the twin verses, earnestness, thought, flowers, the fool, the wise, anger, happiness, the elephant, and thirst.

teach.h: A STORY BEHIND ALMOST EVERY VERSE.
teach.b: An old commentary adds a story for almost every verse, telling who the Buddha was speaking to and why, and some of those stories are coming.
The translation here is the one Max Müller published in 1881, in the Sacred Books of the East.
His English is old-fashioned in places, and when his wording and the Pali part ways, i'll say so. Tomorrow, verse one.

how: In Theravada countries the Dhammapada is memorized, chanted and taught, and some Buddhists know many of its verses by heart; teachers often give a talk on a single verse and the story the commentary tells about it.

games.why: that's the plan for camp four: all twenty-six chapters, in order, a few verses a day.

practice: Here are the twenty-six chapter titles in Müller's English; just listen, and notice which one pulls at you: the twin verses, earnestness, thought, flowers, the fool, the wise man, the venerable, the thousands, evil, punishment, old age, self, the world, the Buddha, happiness, pleasure, anger, impurity, the just, the way, miscellaneous, the downward course, the elephant, thirst, the mendicant, the brahmana.
Which one was yours? Hold that title gently, and let the breath take over.

wordCard.voice: Dhammapada. The path of the dhamma, or the verses of the dhamma: pada means both a step and a line.

orig.note: Pali: dhamma (the teaching) and pada (step, path, line of verse).
